passages.text: It was now just before the Passover Feast, and Jesus knew that His hour had come to leave this world and return to the Father. Having loved His own who were in the world, He loved them to the very end.
passages.sermon:
Jesus is the Son of God.
He knew the time had come for Him to leave this world.
He knew He would return to the Father.
This happened just before the Passover Feast.
Jesus had loved His own people who were in the world.
He loved them completely.
He loved them to the very end.
passages.original: Πρὸ δὲ τῆς ἑορτῆς τοῦ πάσχα εἰδὼς ὁ Ἰησοῦς ὅτι ἦλθεν αὐτοῦ ἡ ὥρα ἵνα μεταβῇ ἐκ τοῦ κόσμου τούτου πρὸς τὸν Πατέρα ἀγαπήσας τοὺς ἰδίους τοὺς ἐν τῷ κόσμῳ εἰς τέλος ἠγάπησεν αὐτούς

passages.text: The evening meal was underway, and the devil had already put into the heart of Judas, the son of Simon Iscariot, to betray Jesus.
passages.sermon:
Jesus was eating the evening meal with His disciples.
Judas was there.
Judas was the son of Simon Iscariot.
The devil had already acted.
The devil had put the plan to betray Jesus into Judas’s heart.
passages.original: καὶ δείπνου γινομένου τοῦ διαβόλου ἤδη βεβληκότος εἰς τὴν καρδίαν ἵνα παραδοῖ αὐτὸν Ἰούδας Σίμωνος Ἰσκαριώτου

passages.text: Jesus knew that the Father had delivered all things into His hands, and that He had come from God and was returning to God.
passages.sermon:
Jesus is the Son of God.
The Father had given Jesus authority over all things.
Jesus knew this.
Jesus knew He had come from God.
Jesus knew He was returning to God.
passages.original: εἰδὼς ὅτι πάντα ἔδωκεν αὐτῷ ὁ Πατὴρ εἰς τὰς χεῖρας καὶ ὅτι ἀπὸ Θεοῦ ἐξῆλθεν καὶ πρὸς τὸν Θεὸν ὑπάγει

passages.text: So He got up from the supper, laid aside His outer garments, and wrapped a towel around His waist.
passages.sermon:
Jesus was at supper with His disciples.
He stood up from the meal.
He took off His outer garments.
He picked up a towel.
He wrapped the towel around His waist.
passages.original: ἐγείρεται ἐκ τοῦ δείπνου καὶ τίθησιν τὰ ἱμάτια καὶ λαβὼν λέντιον διέζωσεν ἑαυτόν

passages.text: After that, He poured water into a basin and began to wash the disciples’ feet and dry them with the towel that was around Him.
passages.sermon:
Jesus is the Son of God.
The Father gave all things into Jesus’ hands.
Jesus came from God.
Jesus was returning to God.
After supper, Jesus poured water into a basin.
He began to wash the feet of His disciples.
He dried their feet with the towel that was around His waist.
passages.original: εἶτα βάλλει ὕδωρ εἰς τὸν νιπτῆρα καὶ ἤρξατο νίπτειν τοὺς πόδας τῶν μαθητῶν καὶ ἐκμάσσειν τῷ λεντίῳ ᾧ ἦν διεζωσμένος

passages.text: He came to Simon Peter, who asked Him, “Lord, are You going to wash my feet?”
passages.sermon:
Jesus is the Lord and Teacher.
Jesus came to Simon Peter.
Simon Peter was one of the disciples.
Simon Peter spoke to Jesus.
Simon Peter asked, "Lord, are you going to wash my feet?"
passages.original: Ἔρχεται οὖν πρὸς Σίμωνα Πέτρον λέγει αὐτῷ Κύριε σύ μου νίπτεις τοὺς πόδας

passages.text: Jesus replied, “You do not realize now what I am doing, but later you will understand.”
passages.sermon: Jesus spoke to Simon Peter.\r\nJesus said, “You do not know what I am doing now.\r\nLater, you will understand.”
passages.original: Ἀπεκρίθη Ἰησοῦς καὶ εἶπεν αὐτῷ Ὃ ἐγὼ ποιῶ σὺ οὐκ οἶδας ἄρτι γνώσῃ δὲ μετὰ ταῦτα

passages.text: “Never shall You wash my feet!” Peter told Him. Jesus answered, “Unless I wash you, you have no part with Me.”
passages.sermon:
Peter spoke to Jesus.
Peter said, “You will never wash my feet.”
Jesus answered Peter.
Jesus said, “Unless I wash you, you have no part with Me.”
passages.original: Λέγει αὐτῷ Πέτρος Οὐ μὴ νίψῃς μου τοὺς πόδας εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα Ἀπεκρίθη Ἰησοῦς αὐτῷ Ἐὰν μὴ νίψω σε οὐκ ἔχεις μέρος μετ’ ἐμοῦ

passages.text: “Then, Lord,” Simon Peter replied, “not only my feet, but my hands and my head as well!”
passages.sermon:
Simon Peter spoke to Jesus.
Simon Peter called Jesus “Lord.”
Simon Peter said, “Do not wash only my feet.”
Simon Peter said, “Wash my hands also.”
Simon Peter said, “Wash my head also.”
passages.original: Λέγει αὐτῷ Σίμων Πέτρος Κύριε μὴ τοὺς πόδας μου μόνον ἀλλὰ καὶ τὰς χεῖρας καὶ τὴν κεφαλήν

passages.text: Jesus told him, “Whoever has already bathed needs only to wash his feet, and he will be completely clean. And you are clean, though not all of you.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to Peter.
Jesus is the Lord and Teacher.
Jesus said, “A person who has bathed is already clean.
He only needs to wash his feet.
That person is completely clean.
You are clean.
But not all of you are clean.”
passages.original: Λέγει αὐτῷ ὁ Ἰησοῦς Ὁ λελουμένος οὐκ ἔχει χρείαν εἰ μὴ τοὺς πόδας νίψασθαι ἀλλ’ ἔστιν καθαρὸς ὅλος καὶ ὑμεῖς καθαροί ἐστε ἀλλ’ οὐχὶ πάντες

passages.text: For He knew who would betray Him. That is why He said, “Not all of you are clean.”
passages.sermon: Jesus knew who would betray Him.\r\nHe said, “Not all of you are clean.”\r\nHe said this because He knew about the betrayer.
passages.original: ᾔδει γὰρ τὸν παραδιδόντα αὐτόν διὰ τοῦτο εἶπεν ὅτι Οὐχὶ πάντες καθαροί ἐστε

passages.text: When Jesus had washed their feet and put on His outer garments, He reclined with them again and asked, “Do you know what I have done for you?
passages.sermon:
Jesus was with His disciples.
Jesus washed the feet of His disciples.
Jesus put on His outer garments.
Jesus sat down with His disciples again.
Jesus spoke to them.
Jesus asked them a question.
Jesus said, “Do you know what I have done for you?”
passages.original: Ὅτε οὖν ἔνιψεν τοὺς πόδας αὐτῶν καὶ ἔλαβεν τὰ ἱμάτια αὐτοῦ καὶ ἀνέπεσεν πάλιν εἶπεν αὐτοῖς Γινώσκετε τί πεποίηκα ὑμῖν

passages.text: You call Me Teacher and Lord, and rightly so, because I am.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
He said, “You call Me Teacher.
You also call Me Lord.
You speak correctly.
I am Teacher.
I am Lord.”
passages.original: ὑμεῖς φωνεῖτέ με Ὁ Διδάσκαλος καὶ ὁ Κύριος καὶ καλῶς λέγετε εἰμὶ γάρ

passages.text: So if I, your Lord and Teacher, have washed your feet, you also should wash one another’s feet.
passages.sermon: Jesus is your Lord and Teacher.\r\nI washed your feet.\r\nYou also should wash one another’s feet.
passages.original: εἰ οὖν ἐγὼ ἔνιψα ὑμῶν τοὺς πόδας ὁ Κύριος καὶ ὁ Διδάσκαλος καὶ ὑμεῖς ὀφείλετε ἀλλήλων νίπτειν τοὺς πόδας

passages.text: I have set you an example so that you should do as I have done for you.
passages.sermon:
Jesus is your Lord and Teacher.
Jesus gave you an example.
Jesus did something for you.
You should do the same for others.
Follow the example Jesus gave you.
passages.original: ὑπόδειγμα γὰρ ἔδωκα ὑμῖν ἵνα καθὼς ἐγὼ ἐποίησα ὑμῖν καὶ ὑμεῖς ποιῆτε

passages.text: Truly, truly, I tell you, no servant is greater than his master, nor is a messenger greater than the one who sent him.
passages.sermon:
Jesus is speaking to His disciples.
Jesus is their Lord and Teacher.
Jesus says, “Truly, truly, I tell you.”
No servant is greater than his master.
No messenger is greater than the one who sent him.
passages.original: ἀμὴν ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν οὐκ ἔστιν δοῦλος μείζων τοῦ κυρίου αὐτοῦ οὐδὲ ἀπόστολος μείζων τοῦ πέμψαντος αὐτόν

passages.text: If you know these things, you will be blessed if you do them.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
He taught them important things.
If you know these things, you understand what Jesus taught.
If you do these things, you obey Jesus.
God will bless you if you do what Jesus taught.
passages.original: εἰ ταῦτα οἴδατε μακάριοί ἐστε ἐὰν ποιῆτε αὐτά

passages.text: I am not speaking about all of you; I know whom I have chosen. But this is to fulfill the Scripture: ‘The one who shares My bread has lifted up his heel against Me.’
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
He said, “I am not speaking about all of you.”
Jesus knew whom He had chosen.
He said this to fulfill the Scripture.
The Scripture says, ‘The one who shares My bread has lifted up his heel against Me.’
passages.original: Οὐ περὶ πάντων ὑμῶν λέγω ἐγὼ οἶδα τίνας ἐξελεξάμην ἀλλ’ ἵνα ἡ γραφὴ πληρωθῇ Ὁ τρώγων μου τὸν ἄρτον ἐπῆρεν ἐπ’ ἐμὲ τὴν πτέρναν αὐτοῦ

passages.text: I am telling you now before it happens, so that when it comes to pass, you will believe that I am He.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
Jesus told them something before it happened.
He wanted them to know this in advance.
He said this so they would believe in Him when it happened.
He wanted them to believe that He is the one He claims to be.
passages.original: ἀπ’ ἄρτι λέγω ὑμῖν πρὸ τοῦ γενέσθαι ἵνα πιστεύσητε ὅταν γένηται ὅτι ἐγώ εἰμι

passages.text: Truly, truly, I tell you, whoever receives the one I send receives Me, and whoever receives Me receives the One who sent Me.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
Jesus said, “I tell you the truth.
Whoever receives the person I send receives Me.
Whoever receives Me receives the One who sent Me.”
passages.original: ἀμὴν ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν ὁ λαμβάνων ἄν τινα πέμψω ἐμὲ λαμβάνει ὁ δὲ ἐμὲ λαμβάνων λαμβάνει τὸν πέμψαντά με

passages.text: After Jesus had said this, He became troubled in spirit and testified, “Truly, truly, I tell you, one of you will betray Me.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
Jesus felt troubled in His spirit.
Jesus gave a testimony.
Jesus said, “Truly, truly, I tell you.
One of you will betray Me.”
passages.original: Ταῦτα εἰπὼν ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἐταράχθη τῷ πνεύματι καὶ ἐμαρτύρησεν καὶ εἶπεν Ἀμὴν ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι εἷς ἐξ ὑμῶν παραδώσει με

passages.text: The disciples looked at one another, perplexed as to which of them He meant.
passages.sermon:
The disciples heard Jesus speak.
Jesus said that one of them would betray Him.
The disciples did not know whom Jesus meant.
The disciples looked at each other.
The disciples felt confused.
passages.original: Ἔβλεπον εἰς ἀλλήλους οἱ μαθηταὶ ἀπορούμενοι περὶ τίνος λέγει

passages.text: One of His disciples, the one whom Jesus loved, was reclining at His side.
passages.sermon:
Jesus had disciples.
One disciple was very close to Jesus.
Jesus loved this disciple.
This disciple was sitting next to Jesus.
passages.original: ἦν ἀνακείμενος εἷς ἐκ τῶν μαθητῶν αὐτοῦ ἐν τῷ κόλπῳ τοῦ Ἰησοῦ ὃν ἠγάπα ὁ Ἰησοῦς

passages.text: So Simon Peter motioned to him to ask Jesus which one He was talking about.
passages.sermon:
Simon Peter was one of Jesus’ disciples.
Simon Peter saw the disciple whom Jesus loved.
Simon Peter made a motion to that disciple.
Simon Peter wanted him to ask Jesus a question.
Simon Peter wanted to know which person Jesus meant.
passages.original: νεύει οὖν τούτῳ Σίμων Πέτρος πυθέσθαι τίς ἂν εἴη περὶ οὗ λέγει

passages.text: Leaning back against Jesus, he asked, “Lord, who is it?”
passages.sermon:
One disciple sat close to Jesus.
Jesus loved this disciple.
This disciple leaned back against Jesus.
He spoke to Jesus.
He said, “Lord, who is it?”
passages.original: ἀναπεσὼν οὖν ἐκεῖνος οὕτως ἐπὶ τὸ στῆθος τοῦ Ἰησοῦ λέγει αὐτῷ Κύριε τίς ἐστιν

passages.text: Jesus answered, “It is the one to whom I give this morsel after I have dipped it.” Then He dipped the morsel and gave it to Judas son of Simon Iscariot.
passages.sermon:
Jesus answered the question.
He said, “It is the one to whom I give this piece of bread after I have dipped it.”
Jesus took a piece of bread.
He dipped the bread.
He gave the bread to Judas.
Judas was the son of Simon Iscariot.
passages.original: Ἀποκρίνεται οὖν ὁ Ἰησοῦς Ἐκεῖνός ἐστιν ᾧ ἐγὼ βάψω τὸ ψωμίον καὶ δώσω αὐτῷ βάψας οὖν τὸ ψωμίον λαμβάνει καὶ δίδωσιν Ἰούδᾳ Σίμωνος Ἰσκαριώτου

passages.text: And when Judas had taken the morsel, Satan entered into him. Then Jesus said to Judas, “What you are about to do, do quickly.”
passages.sermon:
Judas was one of Jesus’ twelve disciples.
Judas took the piece of bread from Jesus.
After Judas took the bread, Satan entered into him.
Jesus spoke to Judas.
Jesus said, “What you are about to do, do quickly.”
passages.original: καὶ μετὰ τὸ ψωμίον τότε εἰσῆλθεν εἰς ἐκεῖνον ὁ Σατανᾶς Λέγει οὖν αὐτῷ ὁ Ἰησοῦς Ὃ ποιεῖς ποίησον τάχιον

passages.text: But no one at the table knew why Jesus had said this to him.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to Judas.
Other people sat at the table with Jesus and Judas.
No one else at the table understood Jesus’ words to Judas.
No one knew the reason Jesus spoke to Judas in that way.
passages.original: τοῦτο δὲ οὐδεὶς ἔγνω τῶν ἀνακειμένων πρὸς τί εἶπεν αὐτῷ

passages.text: Since Judas kept the money bag, some thought that Jesus was telling him to buy what was needed for the feast, or to give something to the poor.
passages.sermon:
Judas kept the money bag.
Some people thought about this.
They thought Jesus was speaking to Judas.
They thought Jesus told Judas to buy what was needed for the feast.
They also thought Jesus might have told Judas to give something to the poor.
passages.original: τινὲς γὰρ ἐδόκουν ἐπεὶ τὸ γλωσσόκομον εἶχεν Ἰούδας ὅτι λέγει αὐτῷ ὁ Ἰησοῦς Ἀγόρασον ὧν χρείαν ἔχομεν εἰς τὴν ἑορτήν ἢ τοῖς πτωχοῖς ἵνα τι δῷ

passages.text: As soon as he had received the morsel, Judas went out into the night.
passages.sermon:
Judas was one of Jesus’ disciples.
Judas received the piece of bread from Jesus.
Judas left immediately after he received it.
Judas went out into the night.
passages.original: λαβὼν οὖν τὸ ψωμίον ἐκεῖνος ἐξῆλθεν εὐθύς ἦν δὲ νύξ

passages.text: When Judas had gone out, Jesus said, “Now the Son of Man is glorified, and God is glorified in Him.
passages.sermon:
Judas left the room.
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
Jesus called Himself the Son of Man.
Jesus said, “Now the Son of Man is glorified.”
Jesus said, “God is glorified in the Son of Man.”
passages.original: Ὅτε οὖν ἐξῆλθεν λέγει Ἰησοῦς Νῦν ἐδοξάσθη ὁ Υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου καὶ ὁ Θεὸς ἐδοξάσθη ἐν αὐτῷ

passages.text: If God is glorified in Him, God will also glorify the Son in Himself—and will glorify Him at once.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke about Himself as the Son of Man.
God is glorified in the Son of Man.
God will also glorify the Son of Man in Himself.
God will glorify the Son of Man immediately.
passages.original: εἰ ὁ Θεὸς ἐδοξάσθη ἐν αὐτῷ καὶ ὁ Θεὸς δοξάσει αὐτὸν ἐν αὑτῷ καὶ εὐθὺς δοξάσει αὐτόν

passages.text: Little children, I am with you only a little while longer. You will look for Me, and as I said to the Jews, so now I say to you: ‘Where I am going, you cannot come.’
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
He called them “little children.”
He said, “I will be with you only a little while longer.”
He said, “You will look for Me.”
He said, “I told the Jews, ‘Where I am going, you cannot come.’”
He said, “Now I say the same to you.”
“You cannot come where I am going.”
passages.original: Τεκνία ἔτι μικρὸν μεθ’ ὑμῶν εἰμι ζητήσετέ με καὶ καθὼς εἶπον τοῖς Ἰουδαίοις ὅτι Ὅπου ἐγὼ ὑπάγω ὑμεῖς οὐ δύνασθε ἐλθεῖν καὶ ὑμῖν λέγω ἄρτι

passages.text: A new commandment I give you: Love one another. As I have loved you, so you also must love one another.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
Jesus gave them a new commandment.
He said, “Love one another.”
Jesus had loved His disciples.
He told them, “As I have loved you, you also must love one another.”
passages.original: Ἐντολὴν καινὴν δίδωμι ὑμῖν ἵνα ἀγαπᾶτε ἀλλήλους καθὼς ἠγάπησα ὑμᾶς ἵνα καὶ ὑμεῖς ἀγαπᾶτε ἀλλήλους

passages.text: By this everyone will know that you are My disciples, if you love one another.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
Jesus gave them a new command.
He told them to love one another.
Jesus said, “If you love one another, everyone will know you are My disciples.”
passages.original: ἐν τούτῳ γνώσονται πάντες ὅτι ἐμοὶ μαθηταί ἐστε ἐὰν ἀγάπην ἔχητε ἐν ἀλλήλοις

passages.text: “Lord, where are You going?” Simon Peter asked. Jesus answered, “Where I am going, you cannot follow Me now, but you will follow later.”
passages.sermon:
Simon Peter spoke to Jesus.
Simon Peter asked, “Lord, where are you going?”
Jesus answered Simon Peter.
Jesus said, “Where I am going, you cannot follow me now.”
Jesus said, “You will follow me later.”
passages.original: Λέγει αὐτῷ Σίμων Πέτρος Κύριε ποῦ ὑπάγεις Ἀπεκρίθη αὐτῷ Ἰησοῦς Ὅπου ὑπάγω οὐ δύνασαί μοι νῦν ἀκολουθῆσαι ἀκολουθήσεις δὲ ὕστερον

passages.text: “Lord,” said Peter, “why can’t I follow You now? I will lay down my life for You.”
passages.sermon:
Peter was a disciple of Jesus.
Peter spoke to Jesus.
Peter said, “Lord, why can’t I follow You now?”
Peter said, “I will lay down my life for You.”
passages.original: Λέγει αὐτῷ ὁ Πέτρος Κύριε διὰ τί οὐ δύναμαί σοι ἀκολουθῆσαι ἄρτι τὴν ψυχήν μου ὑπὲρ σοῦ θήσω

passages.text: “Will you lay down your life for Me?” Jesus replied. “Truly, truly, I tell you, before the rooster crows, you will deny Me three times.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to Peter.
Jesus asked Peter a question.
Jesus said, “Will you lay down your life for Me?”
Jesus gave Peter a truth.
Jesus said, “I tell you the truth.”
Jesus said, “Before the rooster crows, you will deny Me three times.”
passages.original: Ἀποκρίνεται Ἰησοῦς Τὴν ψυχήν σου ὑπὲρ ἐμοῦ θήσεις ἀμὴν ἀμὴν λέγω σοι οὐ μὴ ἀλέκτωρ φωνήσῃ ἕως οὗ ἀρνήσῃ με τρίς
